easy.def: To sleep all winter.
examples: Bears hibernate when it is cold.
The bear hibernates in a cave.
Some bats hibernate all winter.

more.def: To spend the winter in a deep sleep, as some animals do.
examples: Some frogs hibernate in the mud at the bottom of ponds.
Hedgehogs hibernate in piles of leaves.
Animals that hibernate eat a lot in the fall.

easy.def: To go where no one can see you.
examples: Let's hide behind the couch.
The cat hid under the bed.
I hide from my brother.

more.def: To go or put something where it cannot be seen.
examples: Chameleons hide by changing their colors.
Squirrels hide nuts in the ground for winter.
The twins hid behind the curtain until their mom found them.

easy.def: Very ugly.
examples: The monster was hideous.
A hideous mask.
The smell was hideous.

more.def: Extremely ugly or unpleasant.
examples: The monster in the movie was hideous.
He wore a hideous green mask.
The hideous smell made us gag.

easy.def: Far up from the ground.
examples: The tree is high.
A high shelf.
The mountain is high.

more.def: Reaching a long way up, or at a great distance above the ground.
examples: The giraffe ate leaves from the high branches.
We climbed to a high hill and looked at the town.
The kite flew high above the field.

easy.def: Up in the air.
examples: The bird flew high.
Jump high!
She threw it high.

more.def: To or at a place far above the ground.
examples: Eagles soar high above the canyon.
He jumped as high as he could.
The balloon floated high into the sky.

easy.def: To mark words with a bright color so they stand out.
examples: I highlight the words.
She highlighted the page.
He highlighted the date.

more.def: To mark something with a bright color or to make it easy to notice.
examples: I highlighted the key words in yellow.
She highlighted the date on the calendar with a red pen.
The teacher highlighted the most important part of the lesson.

easy.def: The best part of something.
examples: The trip was the highlight of my summer.
The highlight was the cake.
Recess was the highlight of my day.

more.def: The most exciting or important part of something.
examples: The trip to the zoo was the highlight of my week.
The highlight of the show was the magic trick.
Meeting the author was the highlight of the school visit.

related.def: A pen that marks words in a bright color.

easy.def: Very much.
examples: The book is highly rated.
I highly recommend it.
She is highly skilled.

more.def: To a high degree, very.
examples: The book is highly rated by readers.
I highly recommend this movie.
She is a highly skilled swimmer.

easy.def: A title for a prince or princess.
examples: Your Highness, dinner is ready.
The Highness waved.
She called him Your Highness.

more.def: A title used when speaking to a prince or princess.
examples: "Yes, Your Highness," said the servant.
The prince is called His Highness.
The guards bowed to Her Highness.

easy.def: A big, wide road for fast cars.
examples: We drove on the highway.
The highway is busy.
The highway goes to the city.

more.def: A main road, often with several lanes, for fast travel between towns.
examples: We drove on the highway for two hours.
Cars zoomed along the highway.
The highway goes all the way to the coast.

easy.def: A long walk in nature.
examples: We went on a hike.
The hike was long.
We had a hike in the woods.

more.def: A long walk, usually in the hills or the woods.
examples: We went on a hike up the mountain.
The hike took three hours.
We packed lunch for the hike.

easy.def: To go for a long walk in nature.
examples: We hike on Saturdays.
They hiked up the hill.
I want to hike the trail.

more.def: To take a long walk in the countryside.
examples: We hiked up the hill to see the view.
She hikes with her family every weekend.
They hiked through the forest.

easy.def: Very, very funny.
examples: The movie was hilarious.
The clown was hilarious.
The joke is hilarious.

more.def: So funny that it makes you laugh out loud.
examples: The movie was hilarious, and we laughed the whole time.
The clown's tricks were hilarious.
Her story about the dog was hilarious.

easy.def: A piece of land higher than the land around it.
examples: We climb the hill.
The hill is steep.
We sled down the hill.

more.def: A raised area of land that is smaller than a mountain.
examples: We rolled down the grassy hill.
A small house sat on top of the hill.
The bike ride up the hill was hard.

easy.def: A word for a boy or a man.
examples: I gave him a ball.
Dad is here. Say hi to him.
We saw him at the park.

more.def: A word used for a boy, a man, or a male animal when he is not the one doing the action.
examples: The teacher asked him to carry the books to the library.
Our dog is hungry, so I gave him some food.
Everyone cheered for him when he crossed the finish line.

easy.def: Him and not someone else.
examples: He hurt himself.
He made lunch himself.
Max sees himself in the mirror.

more.def: Used to talk about a male person who has just been named, as the one who does or gets the action.
examples: He taught himself to play the guitar.
Jake cut himself a slice of bread.
The old farmer built the barn by himself.

easy.def: A small clue.
examples: Give me a hint.
The hint helped.
I need a hint.

more.def: A small piece of help that gives a clue without telling the whole answer.
examples: Give me a hint about the answer.
The teacher gave a hint about the next question.
A hint of smoke was in the air.

easy.def: The part at the side of your body, near your leg.
examples: I put my hands on my hips.
The hula hoop spun on her hips.
He hurt his hip.

more.def: The part of your body where your leg joins the rest of you, at the side below your waist.
examples: She put her hands on her hips.
He twisted his hips to spin the hula hoop.
Her hip hurt after she fell.

easy.def: A person with a free, peaceful way of life from the 1960s.
examples: The hippie wore flowers.
Hippies liked peace.
He dressed like a hippie.

more.def: A person from the 1960s and 1970s who wore flowery clothes and believed in peace and love.
examples: The hippie wore flowers in her hair.
Hippies often wore bright, loose clothes.
He dressed like a hippie for the party.

easy.def: To pay someone to do a job.
examples: They hired a painter.
The shop hired a helper.
We hired a guide.

more.def: To pay someone to work for you.
examples: The restaurant hired a new cook.
We hired a guide to show us the cave.
The family hired a painter for the house.

easy.def: A word that shows something belongs to a boy or a man.
examples: That is his hat.
His dog is big.
Tom lost his shoe.

more.def: A word used to show that something belongs to or is connected with a boy, a man, or a male animal.
examples: My dad forgot his keys on the kitchen table.
The horse shook his mane in the wind.
Ravi finished his homework before dinner.

easy.def: A person who studies the past.
examples: The historian wrote a book.
A historian knows old events.
The historian visited our class.

more.def: A person who studies and writes about what happened in the past.
examples: The historian wrote a book about the Civil War.
A historian visited our class.
The historian studied old letters.

easy.def: Important in history.
examples: It was a historic day.
A historic house.
We saw a historic place.

more.def: Important or famous in history.
examples: July fourth is a historic day for the country.
We toured a historic house built over two hundred years ago.
The team won a historic victory.

easy.def: Having to do with the past.
examples: It is a historical place.
A historical story.
We visited a historical site.

more.def: Having to do with history, or something that really happened in the past.
examples: The historical museum showed old maps.
The story is based on a historical event.
The museum has historical maps.

easy.def: What happened in the past.
examples: We learn history at school.
I read about the history of our town.
I love history.

more.def: The study of events in the past, or the events themselves.
examples: In history class, we learned about the first explorers.
The museum tells the history of our town.
Her grandmother knows the history of the family.

easy.def: To touch something hard with a quick move.
examples: I hit the ball.
The ball hit the wall.
She hit the drum.

more.def: To strike something with force, usually with your hand or an object.
examples: She hit the ball over the fence with a bat.
The rain hit the window with a loud tap.
He hit the drum in time with the music.

easy.def: To fasten with a hook.
examples: I hitch the horse.
Dad hitched the trailer.
She hitched the sled.

more.def: To fasten something to something else with a hook or rope.
examples: The farmer hitched the horse to the cart.
Dad hitched the trailer to the car.
She hitched her sled to the dog.
